title: What Exercise Really Does to Heart Plaque
description: You can have plaque in your arteries and a healthy heart at the same time. I know that sounds weird, but research suggests that high volumes of exercise can increase coronary artery calcium (CAC), which is hardened plaque in the vessels of your heart. And ordinarily, more calcified plaque and a higher CAC score on cardiac imaging are associated with a greater risk of heart disease . So why would athletes have more calcified plaque? Sounds like a paradox. But it gets weirder! Because even as coronary calcium increases, cardiovascular risk may not… it might even go down. That’s completely the opposite of what we’re taught and seems to defy logic, like a flying hippo. How can more exercise sometimes lead to more plaque in your heart, but not more heart attacks or cardiovascular deaths? Understanding the answer is literally life and death. In fact, it may be the reason I still have a dad. The biology we’re going to discuss may have literally saved his life. I know that sounds like an exaggeration. But it’s not. You’ll see. But let’s get into our first mystery! Paradox #1: When More Exercise Means More Plaque This is one of the most curious paradoxes in exercise physiology. People who perform large volumes of endurance exercise tend to have more CAC than moderately active individuals. To define our terms, when doctors want to know how much plaque is building up in your heart’s arteries, they run a scan that gives you a “coronary artery calcium” score. Think of it like rust in a pipe. More calcium, more buildup. And in the general population, a higher score tracks with a higher risk of heart attacks and death. A CAC of 0, by comparison, is thought of as a warranty against having a heart attack. This has come to be known as the “ Power of Zero.

title: The Cure for Ulcers Is… Cabbages?
description: In 1949, a Stanford doctor published a study reporting on a strange experiment. The doctor, Dr. Garnett Cheney, took patients with ulcers and attempted to treat them with cabbages. Fresh cabbage juice, to be specific. And before you laugh at this ridiculous idea: it worked! Patients with stomach ulcers who drank fresh cabbage juice appeared to heal in just 7 days. For comparison, the typical healing time reported in earlier studies was 42 days. That’s 6 times faster. And we’re not talking about a minor condition. Back then, a stomach ulcer wasn’t just painful. It could cause catastrophic bleeding, perforate your stomach or intestine, and even kill you. So how on earth could something as ordinary as cabbage juice make such a difference? And why is it relevant to you and me 77 years later? Credit to Niba Nirmal B.S. for inspiring this article. Here, we build on that inspiration with a deeper dive into the biology, potential implications for human health, and practical takeaways. Let’s complete our opening story and reveal the early logic of this unusual treatment. Cheney had previously experimented with guinea pigs and found that cabbage leaves appeared to protect against experimentally induced ulcers. So, he decided to try something similar in humans. He recruited 13 patients with peptic ulcers and had them drink approximately 1 liter of fresh cabbage juice every day . The seven patients with duodenal ulcers , meaning ulcers in the first part of the small intestine, healed in an average of 10.4 days. In earlier studies, the average was about 37 days. The six patients with gastric ulcers , meaning ulcers in the stomach itself, healed in an average of just 7.3 days, which as we noted above, was about 6 times faster than the historical comparison of 42 days.

title: How to Reduce Liver Fat by 68% in 6 Months (Proven in RCTs)
description: Fatty liver affects roughly 1 in 3 adults. And it’s a serious, insidious health problem because your liver is the gatekeeper of your metabolism. When your liver accumulates excess fat, it can become insulin resistant, setting the stage for cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and dementia. And the issue is that most people are getting terrible nutrition advice for fatty liver. The result? Many people’s fatty liver progresses when it can, and should, regress. Yes, fatty liver can absolutely be reversed. And fast! In fact, one recent randomized controlled trial showed that a specific diet could reduce liver fat by 68% in just six months. We will get into it. But first, we need to understand why the liver gets fatty in the first place. (Hint: it’s not because you ate fat.) Why Does a Liver Get Fatty? A liver becomes fatty when the fat being produced outpaces the fat being burned. I do emphasize “being produced” because the primary culprit in fatty liver is not the butter you fried your eggs in that migrated into your liver and popped a squat. Rather, fatty liver arises when your liver makes its own new fat particularly from sugar and refined carbohydrate in the diet (a process called de novo lipogenesis ). As for the other side of the equation, fat is burned largely on demand. So, the high-level formula to reverse fatty liver is: Press the brake on de novo lipogenesis through reducing the driving dietary force. Pressing the gas on liver fat burning by creating the right metabolic conditions. Or, if you want to think about your liver like a bathtub. The fat stored in your liver is the water level. Eating more sugar and refined carbohydrates is like turning on the faucet, increasing the flow of fat into the liver.
